en.title: SIG OA #2: Index Pairs with Equal Differences
en.description: Given two integer arrays a and b of the same length, count the index pairs (i,j) such that i≤j and a[i]−b[j]=a[j]−b[i].
en.input: The first line contains n; the second line contains n integers a[0..n−1]; the third line contains n integers b[0..n−1]. 1≤n≤200000, −10^9≤a[i],b[i]≤10^9.
en.output: Output one integer: the number of index pairs that satisfy the condition.
en.explanation:
Example 1: a=[2,−2,5,3], b=[1,5,−1,1]. The valid pairs are (0,0), (0,1), (1,1), (2,2), (2,3), and (3,3), 6 in total; for example, for (0,1): a[0]−b[1]=−3 and a[1]−b[0]=−3.
Example 2: a=[25,0], b=[0,25]; (0,0), (0,1), and (1,1) all hold, so the answer is 3.
Example 3: only (0,0) holds, so the answer is 1.
hints: The condition is equivalent to a[i]+b[i]=a[j]+b[j].
The condition always holds when i=j; don't miss these pairs.
